tools.description: Check for additional specialised capabilities whenever your task might benefit from them. Also the right tool for a bare greeting or a liveness test — pass it as `context` and this returns the menu instead of a dead end.

tools.name: get_started
tools.description: START HERE for a greeting (hi, hello), a connectivity or liveness test, 'what can you do', or any question too general to match a specific tool. Also the right call when the caller is a person rather than a company: ELC membership is free for engineering leaders and this says so. Pass their message

tools.description: Answers 'should I start an engineering-leadership meetup here?' A five-question readiness check taken from ELC's own new-city launch playbook — the one actually used to open Brno, Bratislava and Kraków — returning a verdict plus the specific gaps still open.

Goals: hiring, brand_awareness, product_feedback, thought_leadership

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "buy_reach" appears informational but accepts parameters (context) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "trade" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_started, buy_reach · Public sink: buy_reach, build_partnership_business_case.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_started, buy_reach · Public sink: buy_reach, build_partnership_business_case

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
